mechanism: The vendor alta_bram9k write mask is ADDRESS-SELECTED: a narrow PORTA_WIDTH packs several logical sub-words per 18-bit physical row and the block address selects which W-lane window is written (shift = blk[hi:lo]*W + blk[3]; +blk[3] skips physical lanes 8,17 for x4/x2/x1). nextpnr's packer drives only the lowest window (lanes 0..W-1), so a write to any non-lowest address silently keeps its old value. FIX = replicate the logical DataInA bit j onto physical lane (base+j) for every window base, so the address-selected window is always driven by a real net.
sim_verification: iverilog against the vendor alta_bram9k model (AG32-Docs tools/vendor_parity/bram_x9_write_multibit_20260913/): unreplicated narrow write -> errors=4 (odd/upper windows read 0); DataIn replicated across every physical window -> errors=0 for ALL native narrow widths x9/x4/x2/x1 (tb_x9_fix_replicate.v, tb_x4_rep.v, tb_x2_rep.v, tb_x1_rep.v). See NARROW_WRITE_FIX_SIMVERIFIED_20260915.md.
implementation: Three coordinated opt-in changes: (1) qin_pack.replicate_narrow_bram_write_datain fans the logical DataInA out to all physical windows pre-nextpnr; (2) the agrv2k packer KEEPS a padded upper DataIn lane that carries a real (non-constant) driver instead of trimming it as a don't-care (constant/dangling padded lanes still trim, so the SERV 512x2 RF stays byte-identical); (3) features/bram.py narrow_write_silently_wrong is self-verifying -- it admits a narrow width only when every address-selected write window is populated by a real net in the routed netlist, so a replication that failed to fill a window stays refused even under the flag.
consequence: Establishes the correctness MECHANISM (errors=0 against the authoritative vendor model) and a self-verifying emit path. Does NOT by itself qualify narrow writes on silicon: each width's composed open image must be board-qualified (SRAM-only, control-first) before any silicon claim. The default build (flag off) keeps the fail-closed P0 refusal and is byte-identical. The prior claim that this needs no nextpnr C++ change was INCORRECT: the packer's active_width padded-lane trim removes the replicated upper lanes unless the packer keeps real-driven ones.
next_experiment: Build an x9 open write image under AGAMEMNON_BRAM_NARROW_WRITE, confirm the routed netlist populates both 9-lane windows (0..8 and 9..17), board-qualify a write that stores to an ODD block address (the window the old packer dropped), then extend to x4/x2/x1.

method: Differential attended SRAM-only board session at X13Y4: x9 UPPER-window write with replication ON (image_rep, DataInA[9] driven from bit0, routed-netlist verified) vs OFF (image_ctl, documented negative), plus a low-window x9 write diagnostic (image_lo, single lane 0, no replication). Firmware writes bit0=1->wl1,0->wl2,1->wl3 then reads DataOutA[9]/[0] back over the MCU boundary. Both sessions control-first, controls PASS both sides, independently audited AUDIT_PASS.
observed: All three arms h_up STUCK at delivered 0 for every wordline (rep and ctl byte-identical; low-window identical): up_matches=2, up_obs=0x00, PASS=0. The read delivers a clean 0 (surrounding bits read 1); the write did NOT store in any arm, including the simplest low-window single-lane case.
consequence: The generic open-flow x9 BRAM write does NOT store on silicon (upper AND low window, with AND without replication). This is the BRAM WRITE-INGRESS frontier, NOT the narrow-write replication: the replication is emit-correct (routed netlist verified, image_rep drives DataInA[9] from bit0) but its silicon effect cannot be witnessed because no generic x9 write stores. Only the SERV x2 dual-port and R9 single-bit writes, over their qualified ingress corridors, have ever stored. Read path delivers. No narrow-write silicon claim; opt-in AGAMEMNON_BRAM_NARROW_WRITE stays experimental and the default guard stays fail-closed.
next_experiment: Solve the generic BRAM write-ingress on silicon (route WeA/AddressA/DataInA to X13Y4 over a silicon-conducting corridor, as SERV x2 does) before any narrow-write board qualification. Then re-run the x9wq differential; only then is the narrow-write replication silicon-witnessable.
